page: Amazon Web Services r8g.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server instance powered by 96 dedicated physical cores of the custom 64-bit ARM-based AWS Graviton4 processor, specifically the Neoverse-V2 model running at 2.8 GHz. It features a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio with no simultaneous multithreading, providing dedicated compute resources per vCPU. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and features a 36 MB L3 cache. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, but provides a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the r8g.metal-24xl demonstrates top-tier performance in multi-core processing and memory subsystem throughput. It achieves top 10% placement in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core metrics. Its DDR5 memory architecture delivers uncached read bandwidth of 481.15 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 218.18 GB/sec, both ranking in the top tier. Database and in-memory operations are highly efficient, with Redis SET operations reaching 198.34 million operations per second and PassMark database operations scoring in the top 10%. Single-core performance is moderate, placing in the middle 50% for stress-ng single-core tests.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal architecture and high memory-to-core ratio offer high resource density for memory-bound applications without hypervisor overhead. This makes the instance highly suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, high-throughput web serving, and memory-intensive enterprise workloads. However, the lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, and the absence of GPU hardware limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, though it maintains strong performance for medium and large LLM text generation inference.
